pr_body:
We have various worker threads, like web server, aclk query, aclk sync, dbengine, etc.

This PR adds worker utilization charts:
1. the % of time the workers are busy
2. the number of jobs done (per job type)
3. the time to execute the jobs (per job type)
4. the number of threads available and busy
5. the total CPU utilization of the threads (by reading `/proc/self/task/<THREAD_ID>/stat` - so only for Linux currently)

The interface is pretty easy and it requires nothing more than just spreading one line of code in select places. The state is maintained in `__thread` variables, so the code is not poluted with anything more than just `worker_is_busy()` and `worker_is_idle()` calls.

The working threads are not slowed down. Only a call to `now_realtime_usec()` and a couple of variables are set by `worker_is_idle()` and `worker_is_busy()`. All the calculations are made by the global statistics thread.

All netdata threads have been adapted to use this interface and their relevant charts are now removed:

- [x] web server threads (the ones responsible for answering agent API dashboard requests)
- [x] aclk host sync threads (one per host database, to sync with netdata cloud
- [x] aclk query threads (the ones responsible for answering netdata cloud queries)
- [x] dbengine query threads (one per dbengine database available - usually just one - there is no way to configure more than one today)
- [x] plugins.d threads (all external plugins)
- [x] streaming receiver threads
- [x] streaming sender threads
- [x] cgroups.plugin threads (both data collection and discovery)
- [x] proc.plugin thread
- [x] statsd.plugin threads (both data collection and flushing)
- [x] tc.plugin thread 
- [x] diskspace.plugin thread
- [x] ML threads (both training and detection)
- [x] timex plugin
- [x] idlejitter plugin
- [x] freebsd plugin
- [x] macos plugin
- [x] health thread

There is also another set of workers, the libuv workers, however it does not seem technically possible to monitor them currently.

Also, in this PR:

`heartbeat()` now tries to spread the threads 250ms to 500ms inside each second. The tick is always the requested (e.g. 1000ms), but instead of all threads being aligned to 000ms of every second, now every thread has a random alignment from 250ms to 500ms within every second. So one thread may count seconds at 1s:300ms, 2s:300ms, etc and another one at 1s:400ms, 2s:400ms, etc. This will allow netdata to trigger k8s throttling a lot less (although not tested).

There was also a bug that is now fixed: `sleep_usec(usec)` guarantees that the thread will sleep for at least `usec` microseconds (it has a loop to make sure this happens). But inside `heartbeat_next()` there was another loop that tried to make sure that the thread will wake up at the required wall time. This had the issue that if you set the clock manually to the past while the threads are waiting at `heartbeat_next()`, the threads would wait until the wall time comes again to the expected time. Now the threads will unfreeze and log an info line to the error log when this happens. Still the behavior of the rest of netdata (eg. the db threads) if this happens is unspecified (we need to test it after merging this PR).

The clocks are now very stable. This is a screenshot before and after:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2662304/167270695-84188aff-2bc7-4a10-913b-de63ac821a8c.png)

These are the jobs executed by `proc.plugin`. Both `proc.plugin` and the global statistics that collect `proc.plugin` metrics are synchronized with `heartbeat()`. Before the changes made in this PR it is obvious that they were not synchronized. The statistics presented show random execution of 1  or 2 iterations for every plugin. After this PR, the statistics are perfectly aligned.

---

Closes: #12748

issue_context.title: [Feat]: add cgroups.plugin discovery thread CPU usage to Netdata Monitoring
issue_context.body:
### Problem

- The "Netdata CGroups Plugin CPU usage" reflects the main thread.
- The discovery thread does a lot of work (finding all cgroups, cgroups name resolution), but we don't track its CPU usage.

### Description

We need to add the CPU usage chart for the discovery thread to "Netdata Monitoring -> cgroups".

### Importance

must have

### Value proposition

Our plugins self statistics are very poor, we need to improve them significantly. Having the CPU  usage chart for the discovery thread will allow us to see how much it contributes to the CPU usage of Netdata.


### Proposed implementation

_No response_
